$comment: Executable receipts for the numbers coding-agent-internals publishes in prose - the page and table counts on the README's first screen and in index.html's JSON-LD, the shape of the twelve agent pages, the benchmark helper scripts, and the star snapshots the pages pin. Every figure that can be recomputed from committed data carries a `check.cmd`; every figure quoted from an upstream project is checked against a committed point-in-time capture of that source under `docs/snapshots/` (URL and fetch date in the file header; freshness is not checked), so the receipt parses the capture and fails if the capture is edited to another value. What stays manual is what no capture can settle: the three live star counts the pages pin, the four pages' unsourced vendor ranges, the price row, and the benchmark tables' hypotheses - each names the missing artifact in `check.manual`. Run with `python3 -m verify_claims --root . run`; CI runs it via .github/workflows/claims.yml. Note what this file is not: the benchmark result tables stay 预期结果 (hypotheses, not measurements) and are listed under `benchmark-expected-results` as manual - nothing here claims a measured number of this project's own.

claims.claim: sitemap.xml parses and lists 18 URLs - the site root, the five dimension pages and the twelve agent pages - each resolving to a committed .md page.
claims.metric: loc entries in sitemap.xml vs the committed page files
claims.method: The sitemap lists the .html rendered form; every slug it names is checked against the committed agents/ and dimensions/ Markdown, so a page cannot be dropped or renamed without the sitemap failing. Parsing the file also proves it is well-formed XML, which is one of this repository's two structural gates.

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import os,xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
ns='{http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9}'
base='https://alloevil.github.io/coding-agent-internals/'
locs=[e.text for e in ET.parse('sitemap.xml').iter(ns+'loc')]
md=lambda u: u[len(base):].replace('.html','.md')
missing=[u for u in locs if u!=base and not os.path.exists(md(u))]
slugs=sorted(md(u) for u in locs if u!=base)
files=sorted('agents/'+f for f in os.listdir('agents'))+sorted('dimensions/'+f for f in os.listdir('dimensions'))
print(len(locs),'urls; missing:',(','.join(missing) or 'none'),'; slugs match committed pages:',slugs==files)"

expect.equals: 18 urls; missing: none ; slugs match committed pages: True

claims.claim: The three star figures the site prints are the snapshots the agent pages pin: index.html's cards show 30.7K / 244.5K / 107K, exactly the rounded 30,667 / 244,530 / 106,920 the omp, Hermes and Gemini CLI pages record as a 2026-09-12 GitHub API reading, and the page footer carries the same date.
claims.metric: the `Stars` row of the three agent pages vs the agent-card labels and footer of index.html
claims.method: Each agent page pins its precise count and read date; index.html abbreviates them. The check re-does the abbreviation (within 0.1K) and requires the same date in the footer, so the two surfaces can no longer disagree about one snapshot. Whether that snapshot still matches the live repository is a separate, manual claim per agent.
claims.evidence: agents/omp.md, agents/hermes.md, agents/gemini-cli.md (Stars rows); index.html (agent cards, footer)

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import re
idx=open('index.html',encoding='utf-8').read()
foot=re.search(r'Last updated: (\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d)',idx).group(1)
out=[]
for p in ('agents/omp.md','agents/hermes.md','agents/gemini-cli.md'):
    t=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
    m=re.search(r'Stars \| ([\d.]+)K（([\d,]+)，(\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d)',t)
    k,n,d=m.groups()
    ok=(k+'K ⭐') in idx and abs(round(int(n.replace(',',''))/1000,1)-float(k))<=0.11 and d==foot
    out.append(p.split('/')[-1]+'='+k+'K('+n+','+d+')'+(' pinned' if ok else ' MISMATCH'))
print('; '.join(out)+'; footer '+foot)"

claims.metric: the release tags, the current release and the PyPI history of hermes-agent
claims.method: The receipt composes three captured registries: the earliest tag in the GitHub releases listing (the list is newest-first, so the last entry is the earliest), the npm publish time of v0.20.6 - the version the page's 当前版本 row carries, whose linked tag v2026.8.27 is the same day - and the earliest upload on PyPI. The check reads a committed snapshot under `docs/snapshots/` - a point-in-time capture of the upstream source fetched 2026-09-14, with its URL and fetch date in the file header. Freshness is not checked: the receipt proves the number this repository publishes is the number the source carried when captured, and it fails if the snapshot is edited to a different value.

claims.claim: Every page in this repository that animates — through CSS animations or transitions, cross-document view transitions, SMIL, requestAnimationFrame or the Web Animations API — also handles prefers-reduced-motion, so a reader who asked their system for less motion gets none.
claims.value: every animated page carries the reduced-motion branch
claims.metric: HTML pages containing a motion primitive vs those containing prefers-reduced-motion
claims.method: The detector enumerates the ways a page can move (animation:, @keyframes, <animate, requestAnimationFrame, .animate(, transition:, @view-transition); a page matching any of them must also contain prefers-reduced-motion. The check also asserts that at least one page matched, so it cannot pass vacuously on a tree that has no animation at all.
claims.repro: python3 -c "import re, pathlib; m=re.compile(r'animation\s*:|@keyframes|transition\s*:|@view-transition'); print([str(p) for p in pathlib.Path('.').rglob('*.html') if m.search(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'))][:5])"

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import re, pathlib
skip = {'.git','node_modules','dist','build','coverage','.venv','__pycache__','.pytest_cache'}
moves = re.compile(r'animation\s*:|@keyframes|<animate\b|requestAnimationFrame|\.animate\(|transition\s*:|@view-transition')
files = [p for p in sorted(pathlib.Path('.').rglob('*.html')) if not (set(p.parts) & skip)]
animated = [p for p in files if moves.search(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'))]
missing = [str(p) for p in animated if 'prefers-reduced-motion' not in p.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')]
assert animated, 'no animated page found: this receipt would pass vacuously'
assert not missing, missing
print('files %d animated %d missing %s' % (len(files), len(animated), missing))"
